summary: A Reed-Muller RM(1,3) error-correction encoder is implemented in SFQ logic using the MIT-LL SFQ5ee process to protect 4-bit messages converted to 8-bit codewords against bit errors in the SFQ-to-CMOS interface. The encoder dissipates 101.5 μW, occupies 0.193 mm², and is evaluated via a JoSIM–MATLAB framework that models process parameter variations and fabrication defects.
motivation: SFQ-to-CMOS data transmission suffers bit errors from flux trapping, process parameter variations, and fabrication defects, yet cooling power and cabling constraints limit the parity bits that can be routed cryogenically.
method: An [8,4,4] linear block code encoder based on XOR gates and delay flip-flops was designed in the SuperTools/ColdFlux RSFQ cell library and simulated with JoSIM; a custom MATLAB framework automated fault injection and performance analysis under $\pm20\%$ process parameter variations and open-circuit faults.
result: At $\pm20\%$ process parameter variations, the RM(1,3) encoder achieved 86.7% probability of error-free transmission of 100 messages versus 80.0% for an encoder-less design; at $\pm15\%$ and lower variations, error correction succeeded with 99.1% probability or higher.
